newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean automakers say parts makers need help.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean automakers say parts makers need help.

text.p: Chief executives of Hyundai Motor Co and other South Korean automakers on Tuesday called for government support of parts makers in the aftermath of Kia Group's troubles.
Hyundai Motor chairman Chung Mong-kyu told reporters the chief executives had agreed to ask the government to ease parts makers' difficulties in discounting promissory notes from Kia Motors Corp.
Kia Motors, one of the nation's top three carmakers, is the flagship unit of the Kia Group.
The chief executives of Hyundai, Daewoo Motor Co and Ssangyong Motor Co met on Tuesday to discuss steps to minimise the impact from the Kia Group's troubles.
"We will request the government to enable promissory notes held by subcontractors of Kia Motors to be discounted," Chung told reporters after the meeting.
He said that most Kia subcontractors also supply parts to other automakers. If they default because of Kia, other automakers would be hurt too, he said.
Chung said Hyundai and Daewoo had never discussed about a possible joint takeover of Kia Motors.

The Kia Group's creditor banks on Monday refused to immediately extend emergency loans to core units of the troubled conglomerate, saying the group's top executives should tender resignations as a precondition for the loans.
But they agreed unanimously to extend their protection period until September 29. They decided on July 15 to offer protection to keep the eighth-largest group from collapsing.
During the two-month protection period, Kia affiliates would be free from servicing on their debts, valued at 9.54 trillion won as of the end of May.
